import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Mathoverflow 21003

Is there any polynomial $f(x, y) \in \mathbb{Q}[x, y]$ such that
$f : \mathbb{Q} \times \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \mathbb{Q}$ is a bijection?

*Reference:* [mathoverflow/21003](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/21003)
asked by user [*Z.H.*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/5098/z-h)
-/

open scoped Polynomial


namespace Mathoverflow21003

/--
Is there any polynomial $f(x, y) \in \mathbb{Q}[x, y]$ such that
$f : \mathbb{Q} \times \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \mathbb{Q}$ is a bijection?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12]
theorem mathoverflow_21003 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ, Function.Bijective fun x ↦ f.eval x := by
  sorry

end Mathoverflow21003

reformulations.difference: The evaluation map has domain `Fin 2 → ℚ`, rather than the source's explicit Cartesian product `ℚ × ℚ`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The equivalence `finTwoArrowEquiv ℚ` sends a valuation x to (x 0, x 1), with inverse (a,b) ↦ ![a,b]. The expression `f.eval x` elaborates to `MvPolynomial.eval x f`, ordinary evaluation of the fixed polynomial f. Precomposition with this equivalence preserves and reflects bijectivity. In `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, I proved the exact existential RHS equivalent both to bijectivity on rational pairs and to existence of one polynomial giving a unique rational pair for every rational output. These proofs do not depend on `sorryAx`.

sources_consulted: https://mathoverflow.net/questions/21003 — question, all three visible answers, and comments.

Giulio Bresciani, A higher dimensional Hilbert irreducibility theorem, arXiv:2101.01090 — introduction, Theorem C, and the polynomial-bijections section; LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/2101.01090.
Bjorn Poonen, Multivariable polynomial injections on rational numbers, arXiv:0902.3961 — introduction, main theorem, and remarks; LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/0902.3961.
https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2019/06/08/ruling-out-polynomial-bijections-over-the-rationals-via-bombieri-lang/ — article, February 2021 update, and relevant January 2021 comments.
review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the source's yes-or-no existence question. Its answer placeholder has the correct scope and polarity. Lean tests confirmed ordinary evaluation, exclusion of zero and constant polynomials, and that the first projection is surjective but not bijective. Bresciani's negative result assumes weak Bombieri–Lang for surfaces; Poonen's conditional positive result concerns injections only. Neither contradicts the recorded open status. All scratch checks compiled successfully, and the reviewed file was left unchanged.
